8ball.title: Donuts at 3am on High Street
8ball.description: Whatever the night turns into, it ends at the 24-hour donut counter across from campus. No plan, no reservation, no defence.
8ball.bonus: Order whatever the person in front of you ordered.

8ball.title: Three Metro Parks, One Day
8ball.description: Columbus has twenty metro parks and they are all free. Pick three at random, drive to all three in one day, and walk at least a mile in each.
8ball.bonus: Let someone else pick the three, sight unseen, and do not renegotiate.

social.title: Hoof Hearted's Short North Taproom
social.description: The cult Ohio brewery with the deliberately ridiculous can art, pouring hazy IPAs out of a Short North bar with none of the seriousness of a tasting room.
social.bonus: Pick your beer purely on the strength of the can artwork.

social.title: A Gig at Ace of Cups
social.description: A small Old North room with a big booking calendar — touring indie and punk acts playing close enough to hear the amps rather than the PA.
social.bonus: Buy something from the merch table of a band you had never heard of before tonight.

social.title: Rooftop at Seventh Son
social.description: The brewery that anchored the Fourth Street revival, with a second-storey rooftop bar behind retractable glass walls and a skyline view through the plants.
social.bonus: Drink a Humulus Nimbus on the roof and admit whether the hype holds.

social.title: Experimental Pours at The Extension
social.description: Land-Grant's small side bar behind the Idea Foundry, built purely to pour the weird one-off batches that never make it into a can.
social.bonus: Order the strangest thing on the board and finish it before you order anything you recognise.

social.title: Comedy Night at the Funny Bone
social.description: A proper club room at Easton with a two-drink minimum and a booking sheet that mixes headliners on tour with local sets you have not heard.
social.bonus: Sit in the front row on purpose and take whatever comes.

social.title: Buckeyes Saturday in the Horseshoe
social.description: One hundred thousand people in Ohio Stadium, the script Ohio at halftime, and a city that shuts down around it — the single biggest thing that happens in Columbus.
social.bonus: Stay for Carmen Ohio after the final whistle and sing it with the arms linked.

social.title: A Show at the Newport Music Hall
social.description: Billed as America's longest continually running rock club, a balconied hall on High Street opposite campus that has hosted almost everyone on the way up.
social.bonus: Watch at least one song from the balcony and one from the floor.

social.title: Distillery Tour and Tasting at Watershed
social.description: An hour through the barrel room, still house and bottling line of the distillery that has been making Columbus bourbon and gin for fifteen years, tasting as you go.
social.bonus: Ask the guide which of their own bottles they actually drink at home.

social.title: Duckpin Bowling at Pins Mechanical
social.description: Duckpin lanes, pinball, foosball and a giant Jenga set across a cavernous Short North bar — the birthplace of a concept that spread to a dozen cities.
social.bonus: Bowl a full duckpin game and keep proper score by hand.

social.title: Beer Garden and Pickleball at Land-Grant
social.description: A 1.5-acre brewery campus in East Franklinton with a huge outdoor beer garden, rotating food trucks and pickleball and basketball courts in the middle of it.
social.bonus: Get a full pickleball game going with people you did not arrive with.

social.title: Blue Jackets Night at Nationwide Arena
social.description: NHL hockey downtown with a cannon that fires on every home goal, and the whole Arena District to spill into afterwards.
social.bonus: Be watching the cannon, not the ice, when the Jackets score.

social.title: Nordecke Night at
social.description: The Crew's supporters' section is a wall of yellow smoke and drums in a purpose-built downtown stadium, from the club that beat MLS's attempt to move it.
social.bonus: Stand in the Nordecke for the full match without sitting down once.

culture.title: COSI's Dinosaur Gallery After the Kids Leave
culture.description: A top-ranked science centre with a permanent American Museum of Natural History dinosaur gallery, and regular adult-only after-hours nights with a bar.
culture.bonus: Go to an adults-only evening rather than a Saturday afternoon.

culture.title: Decode the Wexner Center Building
culture.description: Peter Eisenman's deconstructivist landmark on the Ohio State campus — a building of deliberately colliding grids that houses some of the most adventurous art programming in the Midwest.
culture.bonus: Find the staircase that goes nowhere and stand under it.

culture.title: Tour the Ohio Statehouse
culture.description: One of the oldest working statehouses in the country, a Greek Revival block with a rotunda you can stand directly under on a free guided tour.
culture.bonus: Look straight up in the rotunda and count the sections of the skylight.

culture.title: Short North Gallery Hop
culture.description: The first Saturday of every month, the galleries along High Street open late and the whole Short North turns into one long street party with art in it.
culture.bonus: Talk to an artist about their own work before you leave.

culture.title: The Billy Ireland Cartoon Library
culture.description: The largest collection of comics and cartoon art on earth, free to walk into on the Ohio State campus, with original Calvin and Hobbes and Peanuts strips on the wall.
culture.bonus: Find an original strip by a cartoonist you loved as a kid.

culture.title: Columbus Symphony at the Ohio Theatre
culture.description: A 1928 Spanish-Baroque movie palace saved from demolition and restored to absurd gilded excess, now the symphony's home — the room is half the experience.
culture.bonus: Get there in time to hear the Mighty Morton organ rise out of the pit.

culture.title: Thurber House on a Quiet Afternoon
culture.description: James Thurber's restored family home, the one the ghost got into in his most famous story, now a literary centre you can walk through room by room.
culture.bonus: Read The Night the Bed Fell standing in the room it happened in.

culture.title: An Afternoon at the Columbus Museum of Art
culture.description: A strong early-modern collection and a genuinely good contemporary wing, in a 1931 building with a glass-roofed courtyard worth sitting in on its own.
culture.bonus: Find the George Bellows and work out why Columbus is so proud of him.

adventure.title: Climb the 44-Foot Walls at Vertical Adventures
adventure.description: Fifteen thousand square feet of climbing with walls up to 44 feet, bouldering across two floors, and a giant swing for whoever taps out early.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of the tallest wall in the building on your first visit.

adventure.title: Spend a Day at the Columbus Zoo
adventure.description: Consistently ranked among the best zoos in the country, with a polar bear tundra you view from underwater and a Heart of Africa savanna you walk straight into.
adventure.bonus: Stay at one enclosure long enough to watch an animal do something genuinely surprising.

adventure.title: Paddle Griggs Reservoir at First Light
adventure.description: A long, narrow reservoir on the Scioto with wooded banks on both sides, flat water and almost nobody on it before eight in the morning.
adventure.bonus: Get out on the water before the first motorboat does.

adventure.title: Hike the Ridge Trail at Clear Creek
adventure.description: Ohio's largest nature preserve — a 5,000-acre valley of hemlock ravines and dry ridge prairie with far fewer people in it than Hocking Hills next door.
adventure.bonus: Do the whole ridge without checking how far is left.

adventure.title: Tour the Crystal Rooms at Ohio Caverns
adventure.description: An hour northwest of the city, a limestone cave system full of pure white crystal formations and a 54-degree year-round temperature that makes it perfect in August.
adventure.bonus: Take the longer Natural Wonder tour rather than the short historic one.

adventure.title: Walk the Blackhand Gorge Rail Trail
adventure.description: A paved trail on an old interurban rail bed cut right through a sandstone gorge on the Licking River, with a hand-carved canal towpath still visible in the rock.
adventure.bonus: Find the section where the old canal channel was cut into the cliff face.

adventure.title: Hit the Bays at Topgolf Polaris
adventure.description: Heated, climate-controlled hitting bays with self-scoring balls, food and a full bar — the plan that works whether or not anyone can actually golf.
adventure.bonus: Win one game without using a club you have held before.

adventure.title: Spot the Bison Herd at Battelle Darby Creek
adventure.description: A restored prairie twenty minutes west of downtown with a genuine bison herd grazing it, plus wetlands boardwalks and two state scenic rivers.
adventure.bonus: Find the herd without asking a ranger where they are.

adventure.title: Ice Bumper Cars in Land-Grant's Winter Yard
adventure.description: The brewery's beer garden turns into a winter yard every year with curling lanes and ice bumper cars, which are exactly as stupid and excellent as they sound.
adventure.bonus: Win a curling end against people who also have no idea what they are doing.

adventure.title: Hike to the Shale Bluff Overlook at Highbanks
adventure.description: Follow the ravines of Highbanks Metro Park to a platform on a hundred-foot shale bluff above the Olentangy, past a thousand-year-old earthwork on the way.
adventure.bonus: Find the Adena burial mound on the trail and work out how old it is before you look it up.

adventure.title: Ride the Olentangy Trail Out of Downtown
adventure.description: A paved riverside greenway running north from downtown through the Ohio State campus and out past Clintonville, all of it separated from traffic.
adventure.bonus: Ride until you hit a neighbourhood you have never been to and get food there.

adventure.title: Open-Range Safari at The Wilds
adventure.description: Ten thousand acres of reclaimed strip mine turned into an open-range conservation centre, where rhinos, giraffes and Przewalski's horses roam and you ride out among them.
adventure.bonus: Book the open-air safari transport rather than the enclosed bus, whatever the weather says.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike the Alum Creek Trail System
adventure.description: Central Ohio's best singletrack — miles of stacked loops above Alum Creek Reservoir, graded so you can pick your own level of pain.
adventure.bonus: Ride one loop harder than you meant to, then swim in the reservoir afterwards.

adventure.title: Kayak the Coves of Hoover Reservoir
adventure.description: Three thousand acres of water northeast of the city with quiet fingers and coves to disappear into, and a serious heron and eagle population.
adventure.bonus: Paddle into a cove far enough that you cannot hear a road.

adventure.title: Climb the Outdoor Wall at Scioto Audubon
adventure.description: A 35-foot free public climbing wall in a metro park built on a former scrapyard, five minutes from downtown and open to anyone who brings a harness.
adventure.bonus: Top out one route with the downtown skyline directly behind you.

adventure.title: Hike the Gorge Trail to Old Man's Cave
adventure.description: An hour southeast of Columbus, the Hocking Hills gorge cuts through hemlock and sandstone past waterfalls, recessed caves and a tunnel carved straight through rock.
adventure.bonus: Carry on past Old Man's Cave to Cedar Falls instead of turning back at the car park.

foodie.title: Cream Puff and a Bahama Mama at Schmidt's
foodie.description: Five generations of the Schmidt family in a converted 1886 livery stable in German Village, serving the city's definitive sausage plate and a jumbo cream puff the size of a fist.
foodie.bonus: Finish a whole jumbo cream puff by yourself. No sharing, no excuses.

foodie.title: Pancake Balls at Katalina's
foodie.description: A converted 1920s filling station doing the city's signature breakfast — pancake balls filled with dulce de leche, plus Mexican-leaning plates alongside them.
foodie.bonus: Order the savoury dish you would never normally get at breakfast, then the pancake balls anyway.

foodie.title: Graze Your Way Through North Market
foodie.description: A public market running since 1876 where Jeni's started and thirty-odd merchants now share one floor — built for eating four small things instead of one big one.
foodie.bonus: Eat something from three different stalls and do not repeat a cuisine.

foodie.title: A Scoop of Jeni's Where It Started
foodie.description: Jeni Britton's ice cream began at North Market and grew into a national name; the Columbus scoop shops still get the strange, good flavours first.
foodie.bonus: Order the flavour you would normally skip and finish the whole scoop.

foodie.title: Buckeye Donuts at an Unreasonable Hour
foodie.description: Open around the clock since 1969 across from the Ohio State campus, frying donuts all night and doing a gyro and a full breakfast alongside them.
foodie.bonus: Order both a donut and a gyro in the same visit and eat them in that order.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Veritas
foodie.description: Josh Dalton's downtown counter is the city's reference fine-dining room — a long, precise tasting menu and a wine list built to argue with it.
foodie.bonus: Take the wine pairing and ask the sommelier to explain the one you liked least.

foodie.title: Morning Bun at Fox in the Snow
foodie.description: An Italian Village bakery with no wifi, no laptops and an open kitchen — just a case of egg sandwiches and morning buns that sell out before lunch.
foodie.bonus: Get there early enough that the morning buns are still warm.

foodie.title: Cheesesteak at Marlow's in North Market
foodie.description: One of North Market's newest counters, griddling proper Philly-style cheesesteaks to order in the middle of the market floor.
foodie.bonus: Order it whiz wit and do not apologise for it.

foodie.title: Beer-Paired Dinner at Wolf's Ridge
foodie.description: One of the few breweries in the country whose dining room is the reason to go — a proper kitchen downtown building courses around its own beer.
foodie.bonus: Let the server pair every course with a beer rather than ordering wine.

foodie.title: Pasta and Amaro at Speck Italian Eatery
foodie.description: The easier, louder sibling to Veritas from the same kitchen — handmade pasta, wood-fired plates and a bar list that leans hard into amari.
foodie.bonus: Finish with an amaro you cannot pronounce.

foodie.title: Dinner at Watershed Kitchen + Bar
foodie.description: The restaurant attached to the distillery — a seasonal menu built to sit beside the bourbon being made through the wall, in a big airy room off Grandview.
foodie.bonus: Order a cocktail made with the spirit distilled on the other side of the wall.

foodie.title: Cocktails at Service Bar
foodie.description: Middle West Spirits' in-house restaurant behind the distillery, doing an ambitious small-plates menu and cocktails built on the whiskey made on site.
foodie.bonus: Order the dish on the menu you cannot picture and eat all of it.

chill.title: Sit by the Scioto Mile Fountain
chill.description: A restored riverfront promenade downtown with a 15,000-square-foot interactive fountain, and a skyline reflection that is at its best right after sunset.
chill.bonus: Walk the whole promenade end to end without stopping to look at your phone.

chill.title: Wander the Glasshouses at Franklin Park Conservatory
chill.description: An 1895 Victorian glass palace holding a rainforest, a desert and one of the largest permanent Chihuly glass collections anywhere, set in 88 acres of garden.
chill.bonus: Find every Chihuly piece in the building before you leave.

chill.title: Afternoon in Schiller Park
chill.description: Twenty-three acres of brick-lined German Village green with a pond, a rose garden and an amphitheatre that runs free Shakespeare all summer.
chill.bonus: Check what is on at the amphitheatre and stay for it.

chill.title: Birdwatch the Old Growth at Green Lawn Cemetery
chill.description: Three hundred and sixty acres of Victorian cemetery and old-growth trees that happen to be one of the best spring migration birding spots in Ohio.
chill.bonus: Identify three birds you could not have named before you arrived.

chill.title: A Slow Hour in Goodale Park
chill.description: The city's oldest park, thirty-two acres on the edge of the Short North with a pond, a Victorian shelter house and the best people-watching in Columbus.
chill.bonus: Pick a bench, stay put for a full hour, and notice five things you would have walked past.

chill.title: Stand in the Field of Corn
chill.description: One hundred and nine six-foot concrete ears of corn standing in rows in a suburban park — the strangest and most beloved public artwork in central Ohio.
chill.bonus: Get a photograph that makes it look like a serious monument.

chill.title: Find the Seurat Painting at the Topiary Park
chill.description: The only topiary interpretation of a painting in the world — Seurat's La Grande Jatte rebuilt in clipped yew, fifty-four figures standing on a lawn downtown.
chill.bonus: Stand where the painter would have stood and get the whole composition in one frame.

chill.title: Get Lost in The Book Loft's 32 Rooms
chill.description: Thirty-two rooms of books packed into a pre-Civil War building in German Village that was once a general store, a saloon and a nickelodeon cinema, open until 11pm.
chill.bonus: Buy a book from a room you had to ask directions to find.

chill.title: Cross the Dublin Link at Dusk
chill.description: One of the longest single-tower S-shaped suspension bridges in the world, curving over the Scioto between historic Dublin and Bridge Park, lit up after dark.
chill.bonus: Stand at the apex of the curve and watch the lighting cycle change colour.

chill.title: Walk the Whetstone Park of Roses in Bloom
chill.description: Thirteen acres and twelve thousand rose bushes in Clintonville, free to walk into, and overwhelming for about three weeks every June.
chill.bonus: Find the single best-smelling rose in the garden and make someone else agree.
